the katG315 mutation, a molecular determinant for INH resistance in M. tuberculosis, is highly prevalent worldwide and a new molecular assay for the detection of katG315 was proposed and developed.
katG315 is the common mutation in MDR-TB and XDR-TB and the mutation is necessary to be identified for the rapid detection of MDR-TB.
the prevalence of katG 315 mutation is highly variable in different countries and a new molecular diagnostic method for the detection katG 315 is described.

the development of rapid diagnostic molecular methods targeting the genetic mutations associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which will contribute to the development of new molecular methods for rapid diagnosis and drug resistance testing of M. tuberculosis.

the molecular epidemiology of katG 315 mutation in M. tuberculosis, which is a molecular determinant for resistance to INH and the development of a new molecular method, a loop mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) method for the rapid detection of the mutation.

katG315 mutation as a major molecular determinant for isonizid resistance is highly prevalent in M. tuberculosis.
katG315 mutation could be detected by the molecular methods and the mutation was a molecular determinant for INH resistance in M. tuberculosis.
the detection of katG315 mutations in M. tuberculosis by molecular methods is essential for the early detection and treatment of drug resistant M. tuberculosis.

the katG315 mutation as a genetic marker for the detection of INH resistant TB was a promising molecular method for the rapid and accurate detection of the mutation.

the new molecular method for detection of katG315 mutations in M. tuberculosis was developed and it would be useful to detect the mutation in the clinical specimens and the method would be applied to the clinical specimens in the future.

the katG 315 mutation can be used as a molecular determinant in the detection of the INH resistant M tuberculosis and can be used in the molecular epidemiology of TB.
